messages:
eli (AcmeApp): Hey @support — since yesterday ~17:00 UTC our production started returning 403s for Redwood API calls after we rotated secrets via Vault. We rotated the AppRole secret-id and updated GitHub Actions secrets, but prod still gets 403. Any ideas?

maya (Support): Sorry about that. Can you paste the failing response body / X-Request-Id and confirm whether you rotated the primary API key or a per-service scoped token?

eli (AcmeApp): Response: {"error":"forbidden", "message":"credentials rejected"}  X-Req-Id: rwd_abc123. We use a dynamic key minted by Vault AppRole (role-id + secret-id). We rotated secret-id and updated GH secrets used by our deploy job.

devon (SRE): Quick guesses: (1) running containers still have old env var because the image/deploy didn't re-inject new value; (2) local proxy or sidecar caching the token on disk; (3) edge auth cache mismatch. Can you curl Redwood from a host with the updated secret to validate token itself?

eli (AcmeApp): Verified token via curl from staging box — it succeeds. So token is valid. Only production pods 403. Our deploy job recently changed from `kubectl set env` to `kubectl apply -f` and I suspect secrets weren't propagated to live pods.

maya (Support): That change would explain it. `kubectl apply` updates the deployment manifest but won't restart pods unless the pod template changes (image, env, or annotation).

eli (AcmeApp): Can confirm: `kubectl get deploy myapp -o yaml` shows env var value updated, but pods still have the old env.

devon (SRE): Remediation options: force rollout restart `kubectl rollout restart deployment/myapp -n prod` OR patch the env to force a pod template change, e.g.:

```bash
# force rollout
kubectl rollout restart deployment/myapp -n prod
# or patch env directly
kubectl set env deployment/myapp REDW_KEY=$NEW_KEY -n prod
```

Also check for a Vault Agent or local token file mount — that can keep old creds until the sidecar refreshes.

eli (AcmeApp): I ran `kubectl rollout restart` — most pods restarted and started returning 200s to Redwood, but 2/6 kept 403. Exec'd into one failing pod and ran `env | grep REDW` — it had the old value. So the rollout didn't replace all pods for some reason.

maya (Support): Are those stuck pods on particular nodes? Maybe node drain/cordon prevented replacement. `kubectl describe pod <pod>` may show events.

eli (AcmeApp): Found it — two pods were scheduled on nodes that had taints we recently added; scheduler didn't evict them automatically. Did manual `kubectl set env` on those deployments and they picked up the new token; requests started working.

devon (SRE): Good catch. Follow-ups we recommend:
- Add a deploy smoke test that calls Redwood health endpoint post-deploy.
- When rotating secrets, either trigger a rollout restart or use an annotation like `kubectl patch deployment -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rotated_at":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}'` to force pod replacement.
- Consider short TTL tokens + a Vault Agent sidecar that auto-refreshes to avoid manual rollouts.

eli (AcmeApp): Also had one quirky case where the app process read `/var/run/token` from a local proxy (our sidecar) which still exposed the old token even though env var was correct. Replaced the file and it fixed the last 403.

maya (Support): Thanks for the detailed triage — I've opened internal ticket INC-9153 and linked your notes. Tagging @ops to add a recipe in infra docs for secret rotation rollouts.

ops (Engineering): Will add guidance: sample GH Action to `kubectl set env` or a rollout restart step on secret updates, and a sample `kubectl patch` annotation trick. I'll also document the Vault AppRole lifecycle and common gotchas.

eli (AcmeApp): One more thing — for future rotations is it safe to rotate secret-id frequently? We used a long-lived secret-id previously. Any best-practice?

devon (SRE): Short answer: yes, prefer short-lived credentials + automated refresh (Vault Agent or sidecar). If using GitHub Actions to inject secrets, ensure deploy job triggers a rollout and has a smoke check.

maya (Support): Closing the thread for now — glad rollout + patching fixed it. CC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9153. If anything reoccurs, reopen. :white_check_mark:
